question: Select the correct balanced reaction for CuO + NH₃ → Cu + N₂ + H₂O.
solution:
The correct answer is __**3CuO + 2NH₃ → 3Cu + N₂ + 3H₂O**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The balanced chemical equation is **3CuO + 2NH₃ → 3Cu + N₂ + 3H₂O**.
 
• This reaction involves the reduction of copper(II) oxide (CuO) to copper (Cu) and the oxidation of ammonia (NH₃) to nitrogen gas (N₂).
 
• In the balanced equation, the number of atoms for each element is the same on both sides of the reaction.
 
• Balancing chemical equations is essential to obey the Law of Conservation of Mass.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Copper(II) Oxide (CuO)**

 
 
• Copper(II) oxide, also known as cupric oxide, is an inorganic compound with the formula CuO.
 
• It is a black solid and one of the two stable oxides of copper, the other being Cu₂O or cuprous oxide.
 
• CuO is used as a pigment in ceramics to produce blue, green, and sometimes red glazes.
 
 
 
• **Ammonia (NH₃)**
 
 
• Ammonia is a compound of nitrogen and hydrogen with the formula NH₃.
 
• It is a colorless gas with a characteristic pungent smell and is a common nitrogenous waste, particularly among aquatic organisms.
 
• Ammonia is also used as a precursor to food and fertilizers.
 
 
 
• **Balancing Chemical Equations**
 
 
• Balancing chemical equations is the process of ensuring that the number of atoms for each element is the same on both sides of the equation.
 
• This is necessary to satisfy the Law of Conservation of Mass, which states that mass in an isolated system is neither created nor destroyed by chemical reactions or physical transformations.
 
• To balance a chemical equation, one must make sure that the same number of atoms of each element are present on both the reactant and product sides of the equation.
 
 
 
• **Redox Reactions**
 
 
• Redox reactions involve the transfer of electrons between two species.
 
• An oxidation reaction is where a substance loses electrons, and a reduction reaction is where a substance gains electrons.
 
• In the given reaction, CuO is reduced to Cu, and NH₃ is oxidized to N₂.
